summary: This is Snowflake reference documentation for the CREATE ACCOUNT SQL command, which creates a new account in an organization. It lists the syntax, required parameters (account name, admin name, admin password or RSA key, email, edition), and optional parameters (first/last name, must-change-password, region group, region, comment). It also covers the ORGADMIN access requirement, usage notes such as the 25-account default limit and DNS propagation delay, and two example statements.
one_line: Snowflake reference for the CREATE ACCOUNT command, which creates a new account within an organization and its parameters.
key_facts: The CREATE ACCOUNT command creates a new account in your organization.
Only organization administrators (users with the ORGADMIN role) can execute the CREATE ACCOUNT command.
The account name must be unique within an organization, regardless of which Snowflake Region the account is in.
The account name must start with an alphabetic character and cannot contain spaces or special characters except underscores.
ADMIN_NAME specifies the login name of the initial administrative user, who is granted the ACCOUNTADMIN role in the new account.
ADMIN_PASSWORD or ADMIN_RSA_PUBLIC_KEY must be specified; the password is optional if ADMIN_RSA_PUBLIC_KEY is specified.
EMAIL specifies the email address of the initial administrative user and is used to send any notifications about the account.
EDITION accepts STANDARD, ENTERPRISE, or BUSINESS_CRITICAL.
MUST_CHANGE_PASSWORD defaults to FALSE and specifies whether the new administrative user must change their password upon first login.
REGION_GROUP defaults to the current region group; REGION defaults to the current Snowflake Region.
By default, the maximum number of accounts in an organization cannot exceed 25, and this limit can be raised by contacting Snowflake Support.
It takes about 30 seconds for DNS changes to propagate before a newly created account can be accessed.
